name: Realism
description: A novelistic tradition, dating from the mid-19th century, that sought to represent society and human psychology through precise observation. It is the common point of departure that 20th-century literature both inherited and rebelled against.

name: Symbolism
description: A poetic movement that began with Baudelaire and spread through France and Russia. Rather than stating the idea behind an object directly, it evokes that idea through suggestion and musicality.

name: Modern drama
description: Prose-realist theatre opened up by Ibsen and Chekhov. It turned the stage into a laboratory for social problems and inner life, shaping the grammar of 20th-century drama.

name: Modernism
description: An international movement that reinvented the very form of narrative and poetry around the First World War. Its tools were stream of consciousness, fragmentation, mythic structure, and linguistic experiment.

name: Acmeism
description: A Silver Age poetic movement that set clear imagery and poetic craftsmanship against the ambiguity of Russian Symbolism.

name: Harlem Renaissance
description: A Black literary and artistic movement that flowered in 1920s Harlem, New York. It raised Black vernacular speech and folklore to the level of literary language.

name: Lost Generation
description: A group of American writers who gathered in Paris after the First World War. They translated the disillusionment left by the war into a new, restrained style.

name: Guinhoe
description: A modernist literary coterie formed in colonial Korea in 1933. It kept its distance from Enlightenment discourse and proletarian ('tendency') literature, pushing forward urban sensibility and linguistic experimentation.

name: New Sensationism
description: A group in 1920s Japan that championed experiments in sensory style. It sought to transplant the Western avant-garde into Japanese prose.

name: Existentialism
description: A philosophical and literary current, centered on postwar France, that reflected on the absurdity of existence and on freedom and responsibility.

name: Absurdism
description: Postwar literature that gave narrative and theatrical form to the tension between a meaningless world and human beings who demand meaning.

name: Epic theatre
description: A theory of theatre formulated by Brecht. In place of immersion, it uses the alienation (distancing) effect to make the audience think critically about the stage.

name: Nouveau roman
description: A current in 1950s France that dismantled the character- and plot-centered conventions of the novel, experimenting instead with the narration of objects and gaze.

name: Magical realism
description: A narrative mode that describes the marvelous using the grammar of the everyday. It reached its peak in Latin America and became a common language of world literature.

name: Latin American Boom
description: The phenomenon and generation of the 1960s in which the Latin American novel, together with formal experimentation, took the world literary market by storm.

name: Négritude
description: A literary and political movement in which francophone Black intellectuals declared pride in Blackness against colonialism.

name: Postcolonial literature
description: Literature that writes back against the language and gaze of empire, narrating the history and identity of the post-independence era.

name: Postmodernism
description: Late-20th-century literature that interrogated representation and truth claims themselves through metafiction, parody, and genre mixing.

name: Oulipo
description: A Paris-based 'workshop for potential literature' that made mathematical constraint the engine of creation. It served as a testing ground for the paradox that constraint gives birth to freedom.
